## What you will learn

- Transformer, Estimator and Pipeline
- Feature preparation: nulls, categories and vectors
- Train and evaluate a classifier (customer churn)
- Choosing the decision threshold
- Cross-validation, saving models, batch and streaming scoring

---

## When to use MLlib

| | scikit-learn | Spark MLlib |
|-|-------------|-------------|
| Data | Fits in one machine's memory | Distributed, no practical limit |
| Input | NumPy / Pandas | Spark DataFrame |
| Features | A matrix `X` | **One vector column** (`features`) |
| Algorithms | Very broad | The main ones: linear, trees, ensembles, clustering, ALS |

Rule of thumb: if training data fits on one machine, scikit-learn is usually simpler.

---

## Three core concepts

| Concept | What it is | Method |
|---------|-----------|--------|
| **Transformer** | Takes a DataFrame and returns one with new columns | `.transform(df)` |
| **Estimator** | Learns from data and produces a Transformer | `.fit(df)` |
| **Pipeline** | Sequence of stages; itself an Estimator | `.fit(df)` gives a `PipelineModel` |

::: {.callout-important}
Everything learned from data is fitted **on the training set only**. Otherwise, the evaluation is optimistic (*data leakage*). The Pipeline guarantees this.
:::

---

## Feature preparation

| Column | Problem | Stage |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `last_rating`, `monthly_spend` | Nulls | `Imputer` (median) |
| `plan`, `region` | Text | `StringIndexer` + `OneHotEncoder` |
| All | Many columns | `VectorAssembler` |
| Numeric | Different scales | `StandardScaler` |

```python
train, test = customers.randomSplit([0.8, 0.2], seed=42)   # before any preparation

lr = LogisticRegression(featuresCol="features", labelCol="churn", maxIter=50)
pipeline = Pipeline(stages=[imputer, indexer, encoder, assembler, scaler, lr])
model = pipeline.fit(train)
pred  = model.transform(test)
```

---

## Evaluation {.smaller}

| Metric | Question | When it matters |
|--------|----------|-----------------|
| **AUC-ROC** | Does the model rank customers well by risk? | Comparing models, regardless of threshold |
| **AUC-PR** | Same, focused on the positive class | Imbalanced classes |
| **Precision** | Of those flagged as churn, how many were? | Cost of contacting a customer needlessly |
| **Recall** | Of the actual churners, how many did I find? | Cost of losing a customer |
| **Accuracy** | How many did I get right overall? | Misleading with imbalanced classes |

The 0.5 threshold is rarely ideal: choosing it is a **business decision**.

---

## Comparing models

| | Logistic regression | Random Forest | Gradient-Boosted Trees |
|-|---------------------|---------------|------------------------|
| Relationships | Linear | Non-linear | Non-linear |
| Interpretation | Coefficients | Feature importance | Feature importance |
| Training | Fast | Parallel (independent trees) | Sequential (slower) |
| Overfitting risk | Low | Medium | Higher, needs tuning |

::: {.callout-tip}
The most complex model is not automatically the best: always compare against a simple baseline.
:::

---

## Cross-validation

```
  params 1:  [train ][train ][valid ]  -> AUC_1
             [train ][valid ][train ]  -> AUC_2
             [valid ][train ][train ]  -> AUC_3   => mean
  params 2:  ...                                  => mean
```

```python
grid = (ParamGridBuilder()
        .addGrid(lr.regParam, [0.0, 0.01, 0.1])
        .addGrid(lr.elasticNetParam, [0.0, 1.0]).build())
cv = CrossValidator(estimator=pipeline, estimatorParamMaps=grid,
                    evaluator=BinaryClassificationEvaluator(labelCol="churn"),
                    numFolds=3, parallelism=2, seed=42)
best = cv.fit(train).bestModel
```

---

## Save and serve

A saved `PipelineModel` contains **all stages**, so whoever loads it applies the same preparation. It also works on streaming DataFrames.

```python
best.write().overwrite().save(MODEL_PATH)
loaded = PipelineModel.load(MODEL_PATH)

stream = spark.readStream.schema(schema).json(STREAM_IN)
q = (loaded.transform(stream)
     .select("customer_id",
             F.round(vector_to_array("probability")[1], 3).alias("p_churn"))
     .filter("p_churn >= 0.5")
     .writeStream.format("memory").queryName("at_risk")
     .outputMode("append").start())
```
